The welcome email, before anyone gets it

Rendered from emails/welcome/copy.json on 2026-09-11. Nothing has been sent. The automation is written and switched off. Edit the copy file, run node emails/welcome/build.mjs, and this page rebuilds with it.

DRAFT — FOUNDER TO EDIT

The note below is a draft. It claims to be from a specific person, and it should sound like him rather than like a good impression of him. Everything else here can ship as written.

Two things block a real send, and neither is code: the postal address a commercial email has to carry, and which mailbox Reply-To points at.

How it renders

The real HTML, in three frames. Scroll inside any of them.

The fourth frame is the real dark treatment with its media query forced on, so it is the same bytes Apple Mail would render rather than a mock-up of them. Gmail is the one thing no preview can show: it ignores that block entirely and runs its own inversion over the light palette, which is what the light palette is chosen to survive.

In an inbox

A subject line is only ever read in a list, beside a sender name, with the preheader trailing off the end of the row. The sender name is the half that usually decides the open.

  1. Suraj from bingd. I built bingd. Tell me what you think. — Hit reply and it comes straight to me. I read all of them. recommended
  2. Suraj from bingd. Thanks for trying bingd. — Hit reply and it comes straight to me. I read all of them.
  3. Suraj from bingd. A note from Suraj, who made bingd. — Hit reply and it comes straight to me. I read all of them.

Suraj from bingd. reads as a person. bingd. reads as a service, and this email's whole claim is that a person wrote it.

Subject and preheader

Subject · recommended

I built bingd. Tell me what you think.

It asks a question, which is the one thing a subject line can do that makes replying feel like the obvious response rather than an extra step.

The grey line after the subject. Second of three places the reply invitation appears before anybody scrolls.

Where every button actually goes

A directly deep-linkable   B opens the app, with an instruction for the last step   D not currently practical, and refused by the build. Every row below was checked against the repository, and the two marked so were checked against the production database.

CardClassDestinationWhat receives it
founderProfile A https://bingd.app/u/saisurajkan /u/* is in appPaths. Apple's AASA claims it, the Android intent filter claims it, and app/u/[username].tsx renders the profile. FollowControl is in the trailing half of the action row for anybody who is not the reader.
ownProfile B https://bingd.app/u/{{handle}} None reaches Invite friends. The four claimed paths are /u/*, /lists/*, /title/* and /i/*, and none is the Profile tab. /u/<the reader's own handle> resolves to the visitor view of their own profile, which deliberately has no Invite control: ProfileActions leaves the trailing half empty for the reader themselves. AND THE SCREEN IT OPENS HAS NO TAB BAR ON IT. app/u/[username] is a root Stack screen declared beside (tabs) in app/_layout.tsx with headerShown true, and there is no unstable_settings.initialRouteName anywhere in app/, so on a cold start from a Universal Link there is not even a guaranteed route underneath to go back to. The card's first draft said 'tap Profile at the bottom', which named a control the reader cannot see. It now says what the link actually opens, and what that page is good for: a profile URL carries an install button, so it is forwardable as it stands. The attributed invite is named as the better path without the email claiming it can reach it.
founderTitle A https://bingd.app/title/d752c0e8-9376-4aa7-bd71-57a11c8d6cfa /title/* is in appPaths and app/title/[id].tsx receives the id.

Group Picks is D and is why it is a sentence in the note rather than a fourth card: it has no route, no deep link, and it refuses to do anything until the reader follows somebody. A card for it would land on an empty state, on exactly the accounts most likely to hit one.

Plain text

Generated from the same copy, never hand-maintained. A message with no text part is a spam signal, and a hand-written one stops matching the HTML on the second edit. 

{{greeting}}

Thanks for giving bingd. a go. I am Suraj, and at the moment I am the
entire team, so this is genuinely me typing.

I built it because I could never answer “what should I watch”. I had
years of films in my head in no particular order, and every app that
offered to help wanted me to decide whether something was a four or a
four and a half. I cannot do that. But I can always tell you which of
two films I liked more, and it turns out that if you answer that enough
times you end up with a list that is actually yours.

Two honest things. It is early, so you will find rough edges. And bingd.
gets much better once one person you already talk about films with is on
it, because the feed and Group Picks have nothing to show until somebody
is on the other end of them.

Group Picks is my favourite thing in here, for what it is worth. You
choose who is watching tonight and it finds the things you can all agree
on.

If something is confusing, if you love something, or if the thing you
went looking for is not there, just hit reply. It comes straight to me
and I read every one.

— Suraj
Founder, bingd.
my profile on bingd.: https://bingd.app/u/saisurajkan

Still yours to decide

  1. Rewrite the note. Keep the last paragraph. The reply invitation is the reason the email exists; everything else in it is replaceable.
  2. Postal address. Not set. This email asks the reader to invite somebody, which is enough promotional content to read as commercial, and a commercial email carries a physical mailing address. There is no company, so it is a home address or a PO box, and that is your call rather than a default.
  3. From and Reply-To. Resend has one verified domain, auth.bingd.app, so suraj@bingd.app cannot send until bingd.app is added there. Reply-To needs no verification, but it does need a mailbox somebody reads, and the release docs still record hello@bingd.app as unconfirmed for receiving.
  4. The third card’s title. Set to The Wolf of Wall Street, because your bio already makes the joke and it is your number one at 10.0. Swap it for whatever you are actually watching: open the title in bingd., tap Share, paste the link.

Not sent to anybody. Automation written and disabled. One email, one copy file, three destinations, all of them real.
